Kylon's chat app puts AI agents like Codex or Claude on the same team as humans.

Kylon launched a new chat app with AI agents like Codex or Claude being a part of the same team. 

Users on the same team can link an AI agent running on their own computer and let anyone on the team @ mention it in a thread to write code or sort files.

> Agents can pass the next steps of a job to a coworker after finishing their part.

> Apps can be built inside the conversation, like an invoice tracker, and published to their own web address.

> Each agent can keep its own memory, with the team deciding which accounts it can use.

ScaleDown launched three small AI models for in-app Classify, Extract and Summarize jobs.

ScaleDown has launched 3 small AI models for routine in-app jobs: Classify, Extract, and Summarize.

All 3 models have a 1M-token input limit, support text or images, and are accessible through ScaleDown's API, as well as OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, LiteLLM, and LangChain.

> Classify - routes text by assigning user-provided labels, including a probability for each label.

> Extract - can read files, collect the desired data, and output it as JSON fields with a high confidence score.

> Summarize - can read long transcripts or reports and generate a short summary of up to 1,000 tokens.

Elon puts Grok Bot on blast overnight

5 posts
18K engagements
How the argument movedYesterday's media brief was Argon launch day. By late night Elon was RT'ing and quoting Grok Bot demos — music video production, taxes, and employee replacement — and those quotes dominated overnight engagement.
What people are arguing about: Grok Bot as laborElon's tax and "better than an employee" quotes collided with creator demos (music video bots, browser builders). Supporters treat Bot as staff; skeptics ask about accuracy on taxes and long-running agent loops.

"Grok Bot can help with your taxes," quoting a user who dumped four years of returns into a bot.

Elon Musk@elonmusk
Grok @Bot can help with your taxes
Jason Freedman@jasonfreedman· Oct 13
I just gave my a Grokbot four years of past tax returns and financial files. Just a dump of folders and unlabled files.

K-1s, 1099s, mortgage statements, HSA records, and every email with our CPA. 266 files.

I just said, please double check my CPA's work.

A few minutes later, it had found a lot of mistakes.

Mortgage interest left off our 2022 return entirely.

HSA payroll contributions counted twice, four years in a row, which created a penalty tax that never should have existed.

A missing IRA form for Jen that would have cost us.

On this year's return: home office errors, two K-1s missing, an outdated 1099, and startup losses we never claimed.

And a retirement contribution the return already deducted...that we hadn't actually deposited.

I sent it all to our CPA. They sent back an amended return. The bot reviewed that too.

One fix went the wrong direction. The explanation had typos.

Three versions later, all in one afternoon, it said ready to sign.

Just a few hours start to finish. With about 90 seconds of my time and attention required. I was just the meat proxy hitting send as Grokbot watched the replies in my email.

Our CPA is great and turned every fix around the same day.

We chatted afterwards. He wanted to know what I was using - just normal ole' grokbot.

I asked him what he was using? No AI tools.

I set him up with @magnetictax for next season (we're an investor). All CPAs should be using Magnetic Tax or something like it. Every single one.

All individuals should be double checking the work and past work with Grokbot or something like that.

Want to copy the exact the prompt I used? it was just this:

"Please do a thorough review of my taxes and help me understand if my CPA made any mistakes"

"Think deeply"

Or just tag your bot into this thread.

Liquid AI@liquidai· Oct 13
Today we release 𝙻𝙵𝙼𝟸.𝟻-𝟸𝟺𝙱-𝙰𝟸𝙱, the largest 𝙻𝙵𝙼𝟸.𝟻 family member. It is an efficient local model for laptops and PCs to work through multi-step tasks inside popular agent harnesses.

> 24B total parameters, 2B active per token
> Context expanded to 131K tokens
> A 128K-token vocabulary
> 33T pretraining tokens
> It is a reasoning model
> Very easy to fine-tune and customize
> Performs competitively with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a model with ~50% more total and active parameters, on agentic and tool-use tasks.
> Open base and post-trained weights on @huggingface 🤗

PR comments go stale fast and confuse agents — better to fix the source than leave agent-facing workarounds.

lauren@poteto
Replying in a thread
• comments go stale very quickly and confuse agents and people
• they are often used by agents to explain workarounds that would've been better off actually fixing the code instead
• they are not enforceable and waste your agents' tokens

my point is that moving prose (comments, rules, agent.md, skills) into deterministic lint rules, better API design/types, is far more effective, enforceable, and token efficient.

comments are simply a crutch that agents will happily misuse
